title: Z-Tunnel and Microtunnel: the two tunnel layers of Private Access

prose.text: Private Access carries traffic in two layers: a point-to-point Z-Tunnel, and Microtunnels inside it. [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:ztunnel-endpoints]]

prose.label: Z-Tunnel.
prose.text: [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:ztunnel-mutual-tls]] {{second-ztunnel}} Client Connector's Z-Tunnel 1.0 and 2.0 for Internet & SaaS are a different subject: [[zcc.z-tunnel]].

prose.label: Microtunnel.
prose.text: [[zpa.troubleshooting.access-path:mtunnel-path]] {{edges-manage-mtunnels}} [[zpa.private-service-edges.data-path:mtunnel-stitching]] {{mpls-analogy}} The Public Service Edge that sets an M-Tunnel up is [[zpa.public-service-edges.what-it-is:control-service-edge]].

checks.do: When an application resolves to an unexpected address on a Private Access client, check whether it is the synthetic IP Client Connector returned rather than the server's address.

second-ztunnel.statement: An additional Z-Tunnel is created between Zscaler Client Connector and a Public Service Edge, or between an App Connector and a Private Service Edge, to support multi-tenancy: Client Connector establishes a Z-Tunnel with the tenant and a separate one with the partner tenant, and the second works without additional setup.

quotes: An additional Z-Tunnel is created between Zscaler Client Connector and a Public Service Edge, or between an App Connector and a Private Service Edge, to support multi-tenancy in Zscaler Client Connector.
This allows Zscaler Client Connector to establish a Z-Tunnel with the tenant and establish a separate Z-Tunnel with the partner tenant.
The second Z-Tunnel works without any additional setup or configuration.

edges-manage-mtunnels.statement: Public and Private Service Edges create and manage Microtunnels, including authentication, policy, setup, teardown and data forwarding; M-Tunnels are end-to-end encrypted connections designed to keep all traffic separate.

quotes: Creating and managing Microtunnels (M-Tunnels), including authentication, policy, setup, teardown, and data forwarding.
are end-to-end encrypted connections designed to ensure that all traffic stays separate.

mpls-analogy.statement: The tags created by Client Connector and the App Connector work like the label stack of an MPLS network: as a label-switched path identifies a connection, the tags identify a unique connection for each application request.

quotes: the combination of tags created by Zscaler Client Connector and the App Connector function similarly to the label stack in a Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) network.
Zscaler Client Connector and App Connector tags identify a unique connection for each application request.
Just as in an MPLS network, where the label-switched path (LSP) uniquely identifies a connection

zcc-intercepts.statement: An organization can specify whether resources must go through Private Access at all times, only on an untrusted network, or never.

quotes: an organization can specify if resources must go through Private Access at all times, when on an untrusted network only, or never.

synthetic-ip.statement: Client Connector associates permitted internal applications with a set of synthetic IP addresses: when a client application sends a DNS request for a domain protected by Private Access, Client Connector intercepts it and answers with the synthetic IP address associated with that application.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector associates permitted internal applications with a set of synthetic IP addresses.
Zscaler Client Connector then intercepts the DNS request and delivers a DNS response to the client application that uses the synthetic IP address associated with the internal application.

client-never-sees-app-ip.statement: The client application therefore connects to a synthetic address and is never given the application server's real IP: the DNS answer is synthetic and the M-Tunnel passes no IP identification data along its path.
client-never-sees-app-ip.conditions: Combines the DNS interception and M-Tunnel descriptions; no source states it as one sentence.
